SHEET 01AboutPROFILE / SUMMARY

I'm an Electronics and Communication Engineering student building at the intersection of hardware and software — from gate-level digital design to firmware running on real boards to the cloud layer that makes a device useful.

My work spans embedded firmware on ESP32 and STM32 platforms, digital design in Verilog with formal verification discipline, and network simulation research into secure vehicular routing protocols. I care about systems that are correct at the signal level and usable at the product level.

Currently a Research Intern at IIIT Kottayam working on trust-based VANET routing, following a hardware-focused internship at NIT Warangal building a multi-user healthcare monitoring platform end to end — custom PCB, firmware, and cloud dashboard.

SHEET 03ProjectsSELECTED WORK
DOC.001 · VERILOG / RTL
Dual-Clock Asynchronous FIFO
VerilogCDCGray CodeGTKWave
A parameterized dual-clock asynchronous FIFO supporting fully independent read and write clock domains — the kind of block that sits between two clock islands on almost any real SoC or FPGA design.
Hardware Stack

Verilog RTL, dual clock-domain architecture, parameterized depth/width

Verification

Self-checking testbench in ModelSim, waveform inspection in GTKWave

Core Technique

Gray code pointer synchronization with two-flip-flop synchronizers for metastability mitigation

Coverage

Overflow, underflow, pointer synchronization and data integrity checks

View Repository →
DOC.002 · EMBEDDED / IOT
Wearable Multi-Parameter Health Monitoring System
ESP32Embedded CI²CFirebase
An ESP32-based wearable that fuses ECG, SpO₂, heart rate, body temperature and motion sensing into a single low-power device with wireless output.
Firmware

Embedded C, multi-sensor acquisition over I²C and ADC interfaces

Power

Regulated LiPo power subsystem with battery management

Output

OLED local display, Wi-Fi / Bluetooth transmission to host

Protocols

I²C, ADC, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi

View Repository →
DOC.003 · DIGITAL LOGIC
Digital Clock — Sequential Logic Design
CountersFlip-Flops7-Segment
A ground-up digital clock built from discrete logic — counters, flip-flops and logic gates driving seven-segment displays for accurate timekeeping, without a microcontroller in the loop.
Architecture

Synchronous counter chain with cascaded flip-flop stages

Output

Seven-segment display driving via combinational decode logic

Domain

Pure digital electronics — no software layer
